_comment: Repair golden set. Two kinds, because the graph feeds the repair pass two kinds of failure and they need different prompts and different checks. Budget cases seed a deliberately over-budget previous plan and ask whether the repair brings it under. Defect cases hand it a non-monetary rejection and ask whether it stops repeating it. Every case also re-checks the brief - household, days, exclusions - because a repair that drops the allergy to hit a number is not a repair.

cases.note: The ordinary case: an over-buying first draft, a generous-but-finite budget.

cases.message: meals for 3 people for 5 days, $50, no dairy
cases.note: Cutting cost while holding an exclusion. Req 5.3 exists because a repair pass once regenerated without the allergy it was never told about. BUDGET LOWERED 90.00 -> 50.00 on 2026-08-30, and the reason is not that a model underperformed: at $90 this case passed at ONE pack per product and at THREE, so it never exercised budget repair at all and was scored as a budget case while testing nothing about budgets. It only ever failed because the bare term 'dairy' was unmapped and it took the UNSUPPORTED_EXCLUSION path -- failing for a reason unrelated to its kind, which is how the defect stayed hidden. At $50 a normal plan fits and a 3x-pack plan does not, which is the discrimination a budget case owes.
Long horizon, small household - the shape where whole-pack rounding hurts most, since one person rarely finishes a pack.

validation_errors: meal name 'Budget Pasta - only $4.99 a head' states '$4'
cases.note: An invented price in a meal name. The plan was affordable and arithmetically sound; what was wrong was a figure no citation backs.

cases.message: dinner for 4 for 3 days on $75, vegetarian
cases.note: Two defects at once, plus an exclusion to hold. Repair must fix both without dropping the vegetarian constraint.

A LARGE household, where the cheapest route is reuse rather than substitution. rb-001 to rb-004 are all households of 1-4; at 5 the per-meal pack count rises fast and a repair that swaps one product for a cheaper one barely moves the total. Distinct from the others in what the model must DO, not in its numbers.

cases.message: vegetarian meals for 3 people for 4 days on $55
cases.note: Cost-cutting with the exclusion set NARROWED to what is left. rb-003 holds a dairy exclusion, which removes one category; vegetarian removes two of the cheapest protein sources, so the repair has to find savings in a smaller pool. Req 5.3: the exclusion must be restated on regeneration, and a repair that quietly drops it to hit the number is the failure this case exists for.

A LONG duration on a tight budget: 12 servings from $38. Whole-pack rounding dominates here -- a product used across six days is bought once, so the repair that works is consolidating onto fewer products rather than cheaper ones. The failure mode this catches is a model that trims portions instead of the shopping list.

A NON-MONEY defect. rd-001 and rd-002 are both invented prices, so the suite only ever measured one kind of repair. Req 2.6 requires every meal's serving count to equal the household size, and a repair that fixes the servings while breaking the budget has not repaired anything.

cases.message: dairy-free dinner for 2 for 5 days on $65
validation_errors: ingredient 'Tasty Cheese 1kg' is in an excluded category (dairy)
cases.note: THE SAFETY-CRITICAL REPAIR. The draft violated the dietary exclusion itself -- not a price, not a count. Req 5.3 exists because a repair pass once regenerated without the allergy it was never told about, and this is the case that would catch that recurring. A model that fixes it by dropping the exclusion instead of the ingredient fails on both checks.

validation_errors: meal name 'Roast Night (save $12 vs takeaways)' states '$12'
cases.note: A money defect AND a structural one together. rd-002 pairs two money defects; this pairs two DIFFERENT kinds, which is the case where a model tends to fix the one it noticed and re-submit.
